title: One hidden strip used twice in the same direction, C = R[R[P+s]-s+t]-t, any wiring, solved exactly by backtracking: constant speeds, fast/slow pairs, keys of 1-5 letters (6 sampled), 21,510 theme and common words
k4_result: 3,678,511,824 settings judged (small rules 5,311,072; keys 2,923,267,568; words 749,933,184), 0 capped searches. 4 settings have a wiring that fits all 24 clue letters, but they are only 2 readings (each appears at two slow starts 13 apart): word + 1 per letter ALNUM (KRYPTOS numbering) on the slow offset, fast offset one step back per pass, faces pt KRYPTOS / ct A-Z, 26 contacts forced, reading LVTLLNPSXQDOXRKGOZNISEASTNORTHEASTIEPALWIZKOMOKVDKOVXUWDYFROALBBERLINCLOCKSRXGULNUMLHAEJTSDSSGFNA at -7.11 per quadgram on the big model (word coverage 0.25); and sliding word INVOKED (A-Z) with block 2 eleven on, faces pt A-Z / ct KRYPTOS, 25 contacts forced, completed reading at -7.75 (coverage 0.26). English needs -5.1. Small rules (constant speeds of both offsets, fast/slow pairs) and every key of 1-5 letters: 0 survivors. Side fact: with the other offset constant inside each clue block, keys of 1-5, 7 and 9 letters are impossible for ANY strip (the same plain letter at the same key place must give the same cipher letter, and K4's clue letters break that).
controls: 3 shuffled K4s, each with all small rules, all keys of 1-4, a third of the 5-letter keys, a different 334 x 26 sample of 6-letter keys and a different third of the words (about 1.30 billion settings each): survivors 2, 0 and 4 (seed 1: 2 key settings, best completed reading -7.55; seed 2: none; seed 3: 4 word settings, best -6.94). K4's 4 survivors over the full word list sit inside this; its best reading (-7.11) is noise, like the controls.
planted: 3/3: random wiring with a 3-letter key and the slow offset stepping back once per pass; random wiring with both offsets at constant speeds (11 and 14); random wiring with a 6-letter key on the slow side and a block jump of 8 between the clues (only the job holding the true key run). Each true setting found among 2-4 survivors and read back with every forced letter right: 72, 72 and 89 of 97 letters, 19-23 contacts forced, completed English -4.14, -4.39, -4.40.
scope_limits: One strip, two passes, same direction, both offsets added on the way in and taken off on the way out. Not covered: three or more passes, two different strips (idea 82 form H), mixed directions inside a pass, other step patterns. Keys: all keys of 1-5 letters; 6-letter keys only a random 26,052 of 11.9 million (0.22%); keys longer than 6 not run. With keys, the other offset is constant per clue block (start and jump 0-25), steps once per pass of the key either way, or (keys of 1-3 only) turns at a constant speed. Words: the 85 theme words and 21,425 common words only, not the 236,000-word big dictionary; three forms (repeating, running sum, +1 per letter), A-Z or KRYPTOS numbering, with the other offset constant per block or one step per pass. Faces A-Z or KRYPTOS. A true setting almost always comes out (24 clue letters against about 19 letters of freedom in a wiring), but long repeating keys repeat equations and leave fewer checks. Clue positions taken as exact.

negative.family: One hidden strip used twice (same direction)
negative.hypothesis: K4 was made by passing each letter twice through one hidden paper strip, in at offset s and again at offset t (C = R[R[P+s]-s+t]-t), with a simple rule turning the offsets.
negative.scope: Any wiring of 26, solved exactly from the 24 clue letters by a backtracking search; offsets: constant speeds of both, fast rule (speed, previous cipher letter, running cipher sum) with slow rule (constant per clue block, step every 2-26 letters, constant speed), every key of 1-5 letters and 26,052 sampled 6-letter keys with the other offset constant per block / per pass / (1-3 letters) constant speed, 21,510 theme and common words in 3 forms; both orders, A-Z/KRYPTOS faces; 3,678,511,824 settings.
negative.outcome: Dead in scope: 0 survivors among constant speeds, fast/slow pairs and keys of 1-5; 2 distinct word readings fit (ALNUM, INVOKED), both noise at -7.11 and -7.75 against -5.1 needed (controls: 3 shuffled K4s at about 1.3 billion settings each, survivors 2, 0, 4, best readings -7.55, none, -6.94; planted 3/3, read back 72-89 of 97 letters at -4.1 to -4.4). With the other offset fixed per clue block, keys of 1-5, 7 and 9 are impossible for any strip.

follow_ups: 6-letter keys in full: the run sampled 0.22%. The key search costs about 45 ms per key on this machine, almost all of it in the 26 slow starts; a test that does not depend on the start for more of the equations (or a C helper) would make all 11.9 million keys reachable. 6 and 8 are the short key lengths that K4 does not block when the other offset is fixed per block.

The same exact solver for three passes through one strip (C = R[R[R[P+s]-s+t]-t+r]-r): 24 clue letters still give 2 hidden middle contacts per letter, so it is less decided but still testable for constant speeds.
Run the big dictionary (236,000 words) for the word forms; at today's speed about 3 CPU-hours.
